lines.text: You have to put more of the roasted garlic in your potatoes, Jeffrey. You always were a bit of a picky eater.

lines.speaker: Jeffrey
lines.text: I'm not picky, Mom. I just appreciate the balance. And honestly, this is much better than the takeout we had last week.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.text: It is nice to sit down properly. The house feels full when we're both here.

lines.speaker: Jeffrey
lines.text: It does. You know, I was sitting on the patio earlier and I caught a whiff of something—a certain kind of dampness in the air—and it took me straight back to the Bay Area.

lines.speaker: Jeffrey
lines.text: It was definitely the fog. That heavy, grey mist that would roll over the hills so quickly it felt like the world was just shrinking around our backyard.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.text: Oh, I remember those mornings! You used to complain that it ruined your hair, but I loved it. I remember standing by the window with my coffee, watching the grass turn that specific shade of deep emerald. It felt like we were living inside a painting.

lines.speaker: Jeffrey
lines.text: I don't think I ever complained that much. I just remember how quiet everything got. It was like the world held its breath.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.text: It did. It was a very different kind of quiet than we have here now. But it was a good life we had there, too.

lines.speaker: Jeffrey
lines.text: It was. And I’m glad we have these memories. Even when I'm here in LA, working and seeing my girlfriend, I still find myself thinking about those foggy mornings.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.text: She's a lucky girl to have you, and you're lucky to have her. But I'm glad she's not at the table tonight. It's nice to just have our time.

lines.speaker: Jeffrey
lines.text: It is. It's funny, isn't it? We've traveled so far from those hills. From that house to this house.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.text: We have. But the table is still the same, isn't it? It's still about the food, and the company, and the stories.

lines.speaker: Jeffrey
lines.text: Exactly. I really appreciate this, Mom. Just sitting here with you.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.text: I appreciate it too, honey. Pass me that pitcher of water, would you? This is a very good dinner.
